sources.title: One Nation asks donors at $3,000-a-head Sydney fundraiser to accept ‘non-disclosure agreement’
sources.description:
Transparency experts raise concerns about plans to use NDA to gag attendees at event featuring Pauline Hanson in lead-up to NSW election

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation is attempting to gag donors from ever revealing details of discussions at an invite-only, cocktail-dress fundraiser with the party’s senior leadership team, in a move described as a “worrying precedent” for democracy.

Invitations to the “very special evening” at an undisclosed central Sydney venue next Thursday show donors will be charged $3,000 for a “private and very discrete” four-hour event.

sources.title: Australians are yet to see the benefits of AI and datacentres – and US midterms show they could be political kryptonite
sources.description:
Albanese should tread carefully as he struggles to make case for how the new technology will benefit ordinary voters

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

When will Australia see the benefits of the AI and datacentre boom? So far, all we’ve seen is the possibility of changes to copyright which would hurt Australian creatives, special rules about power and water use, and the threat of mass displacement or replacement of workers, with the trade-off being a mere 10% chance of human extinction.

Now add the Reserve Bank’s assessment this week that datacentres were part of growing “inflationary pressures” when lifting interest rates to an 18-year high.

sources.title: ‘Bring it on’: Pauline Hanson to appeal Mehreen Faruqi racial discrimination ruling in high court
sources.description:
One Nation leader granted special leave to appeal after full federal court earlier this year agreed Hanson portrayed Faruqi as a ‘second-class citizen’

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s high court has agreed to hear Pauline Hanson’s appeal against a ruling that she engaged in racial discrimination against Mehreen Faruqi when she told the Greens senator to “pack your bags and piss off back to Pakistan”.

The One Nation leader was granted special leave to appeal on Thursday after the full federal court earlier this year unanimously upheld a 2024 decision.

sources.title: Bomb threats disrupt at least 25 flights across Europe, raising hybrid war fears
sources.description:
Planes forced into emergency landings or diversions two days after hoax alerts affected air travel

  • Europe live – latest updates

Hoax bomb threats have caused at least 25 flights across Europe to be disrupted, with some forced to make emergency landings, as questions mount over an apparently coordinated effort to cause chaos for travellers.

The series of warnings on Thursday affected flights between Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, France, Greece, Serbia and Czechia.

sources.title: Multiple planes diverted as bomb threats to commercial flights reported across Europe – as it happened
sources.description:
EU transport commissioner says ‘too early’ to say if bomb threats to 20 flights are linked

  • Tell us: have you been affected by the bomb threats?

And the Italian news agency Ansa reported that two more planes with links to Italy were affected by bomb threats this morning: that’s a WizzAir service from Milan Malpensa to Warsaw, which reportedly landed in Vienna, and a Finnair flight from Helsinki to Rome Fiumicino.

Belgian newspaper Le Soir also reported a bomb threat against a LOT Polish Airline flight from Warsaw, which now landed at Zaventem.

sources.title: Republicans hoping to succeed Trump in 2028 dissect midterm rout
sources.description:
JD Vance, Ron DeSantis and Ted Cruz all pointed to Iran war and affordability as key factors in Democratic victory

  • US midterms 2026 live – latest updates

Republican hopefuls in the race to succeed Donald Trump swiftly blamed two key pillars of his agenda – the Iran war and tariffs – for summoning the Democratic blue wave that swept the US midterm elections.

The fallout from the stunning success of Democrats on Tuesday night has left Republicans reeling – and grasping for the reasons behind the collapse in support. On Thursday, the Associated Press called more competitive House races for the Democrats, though Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi remained undecided.

sources.title: Harmeet Dhillon, controversial head of DoJ’s civil rights division, steps down
sources.description:
Dhillon is first high-level justice department official to leave after historic Republican defeat in 2026 midterms

  • US midterms 2026 live – latest updates

Harmeet Dhillon, a Donald Trump ally who led the justice department’s civil rights division, is leaving her position.

“Today, I accepted the resignation of Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon, who led the Civil Rights Division with conviction the past 18 months. She has defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor. The Department is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors,” the attorney general, Todd Blanche, said in a post on X.

sources.title: What to Know About the Bomb Threats Disrupting Flights in Europe
sources.description: More than two dozen planes that were targeted on Thursday landed safely, officials said, after similar threats earlier this week. The hoaxes have added to airspace anxiety in the region.
